These writ petitions have been filed by individual petitioners raising challenge to the Bye-laws dated 10.12.2021 notified (on 01.02.2022) by the Municipal Corporation, Bareilly levying Advertisement Fees on hoardings etc. Also, challenge has been raised to individual demand orders issued to the petitioners dated 16.08.2021 in Writ Petition 28984 of 2022 and dated 16.08.2021 in Writ-C No.14655 of 2022. Further, challenge has been raised to the document dated 16.08.2021, whereby the objections raised by the petitioners to the proposed Bye-laws, have been rejected. Last, challenge has been laid to subsequent tender notices.

4. Sectio

A Municipal Corporation constituted under sub-clause (c) of clause (1) of Article 243-Q of the Constitution in accordance with Part IX-A thereof shall be known as the Municipal Corporation of (Name of the city) and be a body corporate.]"

"16. Composition of the Corporation.

6. Sections 541, 543 and 544 of the Act read as below:-
"541. Bye-laws for what purpose to be made. - The Corporation may from time to time make bye-laws, not incon

Bye- laws to be published.

7. In the above statutory context, it is the case of the petitioners that the impugned Bye-law namely the Nagar Nigam, Bareilly (Vigyapano Ka Viniyaman Aur Niyantran Evam Anugyapti Shulk Nirdharan Aur Vasuli) Upvidhi 2020 (hereinafter refer
Thus, it has been submitted:-

Relying on the five judge bench decision of the Supreme Court in Commissioner of Income Tax, Mumbai v. Anjum M.H. Ghaswala and others,
2002(1) SCC 633, it has been submitted, when a statute requires a thing to be done in a particular manner
Objections were never invited in terms of Section 543(a) of the Act.
Thus, neither any Gazette publication was made nor the newspaper/Bulletin publication made, specified the date after which the Bye-law was to be taken into consideration by the Municipal Corporation.

As to lack of publication in the Official Gazette,
reliance has been placed on State of M.P. and another v. Ram Ragubir Prasad Agarwal and others,
AIR 1979 SC 888.
In absence of publication in the Official Gazette, the entire action taken by the respondent is invalid.
As a fact no objections were invited by the Municipal Corporation to the impugned Bye-law, in the manner prescribed.
Therefore, the Bye-law may not have been notified and enforced without prior approval of the Municipal Corporation.
That action has not been performed by the collective body and/ or the body incorporate.
Reference has been made to pleadings made in paragraph nos. 8, 9, 11 and 15 of the Writ Petition.

They read as below:-
"8. That, the proposed byelaws were published on the official website of the Respondent 2 and was published in the newspaper of Dainik Jagaran and Amar Ujala on 16.02.2021 calling for objections and suggestions.

9.

15. That, wholly without any authority of law, the objections taken by Petitioners was decided by Respondent 3 on 16.08.2021 and not by the Corporation, as mandated under law.
Copy of the objections so decided on 16.08.2021 is attached as Annexure-5."
9. Submission is, the objections invited by the Municipal Corporation Bareilly have not been dealt with and decided by that body.

Reply to the above pleadings is contained in paragraph Nos.5, 6 and 7 of the Counter Affidavit of the respondent Corporation filed by Shri Jatin Kuldeep Singh, Prabhari Law, Nagar Nigam, Bareilly.

They read as below:-

A copy of the chart dated 23.06.2021 along with noting dated 16.08.2021 as well as the attendance sheet are all hereby marked collectively as Annexure No. CA-1 to this counter affidavit.

10. Reliance has been placed on a decision of the co-ordinate bench of this Court in U.P. Advertisers Association Vs. State of U.P and 2 Others 2017 (5) ADJ 788.
11.

Shri Sanjeev Singh and Shri Shyam Mani Shukla, learned counsel appearing for the Municipal Corporation would submit, though Gazette publication was not made, at the same time newspaper publication was made on 15/16.02.2021, inviting objecti
Not only such publication was made but the petitioners filed their written objections as is their admitted case.
Therefore, no legal injury has been caused to the petitioners owing to non-publication of notice inviting objection in the official gazette.

12. Second, it has been submitted, the objections filed by the petitioners were dealt with and decided as is clear from a bare perusal of Annexure no.1 to the Counter Affidavit to the writ petition filed by M/s S.S. Graphics.

13. Since the Municipal Board could not have dealt with individual objections, the same were dealt with by a three-member Committee comprising of the Tax Inspector, Assistant Engineer, Nagar Aar Publicity And 6 Others vs State Of U.P. And A
Those were placed before the Municipal Commissioner who accorded his approval, on 16.08.2021.
However, the Bye-law was not enforced pursuant to that decision.

Rather, the matter was placed before the Municipal Board in its meeting on 28.08.2021 wherein it was approved by means of Supplementary Agenda, after recording amendment in terms of the discussion of the Board.
14. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having perused the record, in the first place, it is to be noted that the power to frame and enforced Bye-law is a pure legislative function.
There is no doubt and there can be admitted no possibility of a doubt in that regard.

In the context of that delegated law making function, the State legislature has prescribed a strict requirement on the Municipal Corporation to first invite objections to the proposed Bye-law and second it has prescribed the manner in which
15. To the first part, there is no reservation expressed by the Municipal Corporation.
Thus it admits that the petitioner and others had a perfect right to object to the proposed Bye-law.
As to the manner in which such objections may have been invited, Section 543(a) is crystal clear.
It requires publication of a notice, both in the Official Gazette and in the Bulletin of the Corporation, if any.
Thus, the principal requirement enforced by the Act is to publish the notice inviting objections in the Official Gazette.
Additionally, but not alternatively, if any Bulletin were being published by the Municipal Corporation, it would remain obligated to publish the same in that Bulletin,
as well.

Here,
it is an admitted case that Bareilly Municipal Corporation does not publish a Bulletin of its own.
Therefore, it may have been open to that Municipal Corporation to publish the notice in a newspaper, as well.
However, that compliance would not obviate the pre-existing essential requirement to publish that notice in the Official Gazette.
That first compliance has not been made.
In the context of law making function delegated on the Municipal Corporation, Bareilly, that is incurable defect.
A law whether made by a principal legislature or it's delegate must always arise/enacted and be enforced, strictly in accordance with the fundamental law of the land-the Constitution of India.
Additionally, a delegate must also strictly conform to the tenets of the principal legislation, under which it may act.
Unless that act is performed by the delegate strictly as ordained by the principal legislation, it would remain invalid.
A statutory law once enforced creates the frame work for conduct of human affairs and transactions.
17. The said notice does not specify any date after which Municipal Corporation Bareilly intended to take up the proposed Bye-law i.e. to enforce it.
Therefore, even the Bulletin/newspaper publication remained defective and incomplete.

18. In the context of legislative function being exercised by the Municipal Corporation Bareilly, we recognise that even in the realm of administrative law, a rule exists-a function statutorily prescribed to be performed in a particular way
We also recognise the importance of the publication made in the Official Gazettee as that is the first and irrebuttable evidence of public notification or publication made.
At the same time, in the facts of the present case, we find that the function giving rise to the lis between the parties, is legislative.
For exercise of that legislative function, the principal legislature has enacted Sections 541, 542 and 543(a) and laid a strict procedure to be applied before a valid delegated legislation may arise.

Since publication of the prior notice is required to be made in that Official Gazettee and also in the Bulletin of the Corporation, if any, no bye-law may have come into force without strict prior compliance of this procedure.
In absence of publication made in that Official Gazette, that requirement remained unfulfilled.

No benefit may be drawn by the Municipal Corporation Bareilly on the strength of publication made in the newspaper inasmuch as that publication may only be equated with a publication made in a Bulletin.

20. Third, as to the consideration made to the objection, while we may agree with learned counsel for the respondents that three-member Committee considered the objection and submitted its report to the Municipal Commissioner and that the M
And Another on 22 July, 2024

22. Thus, it is not shown to us that there was any Supplementary Agenda circulated amongst the members of the Municipal Corporation of the Bareilly, informing them about the consideration to be made to the proposed Bye-law or the objections
23. Second, no material-either the objections or the report submitted by the three-member Committee (as approved by the Municipal Commissioner) has been referred to in those minutes.

No intrinsic or extrinsic evidence has been shown to exist as may allow us to entertain any possibility that the proposed Bye-law and the objections filed thereto were either placed before or were considered by the collective body i.e. Muni
Then, in U.P. Advertisers Association (supra), a coordinate bench of this Court had specifically held that no liability to pay tax etc. may be imposed except in accordance with the valid law framed.
Though this is not a case of involving levy of tax at the same time, for reasons noted above, we are not inclined to take any other view in the present facts.
25. The aforesaid writ petitions must succeed.
Accordingly, they are allowed.
The Bye-law is declared to be unconstitutional to the extent valid procedure has not been complied to invite and deal with the objection thereto.
Also, the same has been duly approved by the Municipal Corporation, Bareilly.
However, we leave it open to the Municipal Corporation to act in accordance with law from the stage of inviting fresh objections.
26. Consequentially, the demand orders are quashed.
